fact: 1903年日本处于1902年1月31日生效的英日同盟框架内：该军事同盟1902年1月30日在伦敦签署，背景为对抗俄罗斯帝国，由英国外交大臣Lansdowne勋爵与日本驻英公使林权助代表双方签署，为期20年（至1923年8月17日失效），是1903年日本外交与安全环境的制度基础。

fact: 1899年7月17日《日英通商航海条约》生效后，在日英国臣民改受日本法律管辖、英国在日领事法院同日停止管辖（未结案件除外）；条约口岸旧界限制被突破，外国人进入内地不再需要此前的护照许可——1903年的在日外国人处于条约修订后的新法律环境。

sources.title: Anglo-Japanese Treaty of Commerce and Navigation（Wikipedia条目）
sources.quote: When this treaty became effective, British subjects in Japan became subject to Japanese laws instead of British laws. The jurisdiction of the British Supreme Court for China and Japan, the British Court for Japan under it and consular courts in each treaty port ceased on that date, save for pending cases which were allowed to continue.

sources.title: Beyond the Treaty Limits: Pushing the Boundaries in Meiji Japan（Cobbing, Japanese Studies 2025）
sources.quote: As a result, in 1899 the Treaty Limits were no more, and foreigners no longer needed to obtain passports before venturing inland.

fact: 国立国会图书馆参考服务数据库转引的资料显示：明治30年前后（约1897年），东京砲兵工廠、石川島造船所等重工业男工1日劳动10—11小时、日给30—35钱，当时米价约14—15钱/升（约1.5公斤）——一日工资约合2—3升米，是1903年东京重工业工资的最近参照。

fact: 1900年（明治33年）东京府人口约195万至201万：关西大学研究表列为1,947千人、福生市立図書館资料列为2,014,100人；另一英文著作记载东京人口1898年约140万、1908年超过200万——各口径存在出入，但显示1903年前后东京已是数百万级都市圈的形成期。

fact: 1903年日本实行金本位：1897年《货币法》确立金本位制度，规定纯金0.75克等于1日元，政府以甲午战争对清赔款充作黄金储备，日本由此接入全球金融体系；同年日本银行券改为可兑换金币——1903年的贸易与结算建立在金本位日元之上。

sources.title: Currency Museum, Bank of Japan — History of Currency（日本銀行貨幣博物館）
sources.quote: In 1897, Japan enacted the “Currency Act” to introduce the gold standard system, and stipulated that 0.75 g of gold was equivalent to one yen. The government used reparations paid from China following the Sino-Japanese war as the gold reserve. Through establishing the gold standard system, Japan was integrated into the global economic and financial system. ... In 1897, the convertible Bank of Japan notes, which had been exchangeable for silver coins, were revised to be exchangeable for gold coins.

fact: 1900年代纺织与织物占日本总出口的49.3%—56.7%；横滨港自1900年起生丝约占该港出口总值的60%；生丝在整个二战前时期始终是日本第一大出口商品——1903年的日本出口经济以丝绸产业链为中枢。

sources.title: The Silk Weaving Industry in Early Twentieth-Century Japan（T. Okazaki, CIRJE Discussion Paper 2020-CF-1147）
sources.quote: The percentage of textile and fabric in Japan's total exports was 49.3–56.7% and 10.7–14.4% in the 1900s (Panels A and B of Figure 2).

sources.title: Yokohama | Encyclopedia.com
sources.quote: Yokohama remained the main port for the export of raw silk to the United States. Raw silk accounted for about 60 percent of Yokohama's total export from 1900 onward.

sources.title: EDJ Chapter: Trade Structure of Meiji Japan
sources.quote: Raw silk remained the top Japanese export not just during the Meiji period but in the entire pre-WW2 period.

fact: 至1900年前后，三井家族通过金融、矿山、贸易等业务控制数百家企业，以家族血缘而非正式契约联结的财阀（zaibatsu）形态已经成形；三井物产在生丝、棉纱、煤炭、大米出口中占据主导——1903年的外贸创业者面对的是财阀主导的分销格局。

sources.title: Reference For Business: Shoei Utsuda 1943—（Mitsui Zaibatsu条目）
sources.quote: By 1900 the Mitsui family owned hundreds of companies, all united by family rather than formal agreements. This system was known as a zaibatsu.

sources.title: Masuda Takashi（Wikipedia条目，引述其三井物产经历）
sources.quote: In 1876, at the age of 29, Masuda was appointed the president of Mitsui Trading Company (Mitsui Bussan Kaisha) and contributed to the development of the Mitsui zaibatsu. Mitsui quickly became a dominant player in Japanese exports of silk cloth and thread, cotton, coal, and rice, and in the imports of cotton and other raw materials.
